record: TI2026 project closure: what was predicted, what happened, and what it supports

production_leakage_declarations.status: unmodified; these describe the production run and remain true

one_event_caveat: realized above expectation is a descriptive fact about one tournament. It is not evidence of calibration, of generalization, or that the model is better than it forecast. N = 1

definitions.OFFICIAL_CORRECT_PATH_EXACT: credited, and the realized participants were exactly the ones predicted
definitions.OFFICIAL_CORRECT_PATH_DIVERGED: credited even though the realized participants were not the ones predicted - the selected team reached this node by a different route than forecast, and still won it
definitions.OFFICIAL_WRONG_LOCAL_PATH_EXACT: not credited, the participants were exactly as predicted, and the selected team lost. A genuine local winner error with no upstream excuse - a root miss
definitions.OFFICIAL_WRONG_LOCAL_PATH_DIVERGED: not credited, but the selected team did play this node - it lost to an opponent that an upstream miss had substituted. Part local, part inherited
definitions.OFFICIAL_WRONG_PROPAGATED: not credited, and the selected team was not one of the two teams that actually played this node. The error is entirely inherited from an upstream path miss

path_error_taxonomy.authority: the official 8 of 14 stands regardless of this taxonomy. The taxonomy explains the count; it can never revise it

exact_matchup_diagnostic.definition: nodes where the predicted participant pair AND the winner were both right
exact_matchup_diagnostic.why_it_is_kept: it separates 'the model called the winner' from 'the model called the whole path', which is the quantity the bracket propagation destroys

uninformed_baseline.why_it_is_here: a proper score is only readable against a reference. This is the weakest honest one. Beating it on 14 series is not a significant result and is not claimed as one

proper_scores.estimator: POINT ESTIMATE from the single frozen serve state
proper_scores.caveat: 14 series. This supports descriptive statements only. It cannot support a calibration claim, a comparison against another model, or any parameter change.

optimiser_comparators.note: this is the slate that was actually submitted
also the recorded second-best-overall slate; differs from the primary only at selection 810
take the model favourite at every node in bracket order

optimiser_comparators.comparator: best slate with a different champion

optimiser_comparators.note: ex-post upper bound, not an available strategy

submitted_slate_rank.tie_handling: realized score is a coarse integer scale, so many slates tie. A unique rank is not defined and is not invented: the interval and the tie count are reported instead

scoring_specification_check.production_scoring_functional: count the nodes at which the slate's winner equals the outcome's winner, then look that count up in the committed 15-entry scoring vector
scoring_specification_check.client_settlement_semantics: the client credits a node when the selected team won that node's realized series
scoring_specification_check.evidence: the recomputation under the production functional reproduces the first-party in-client settlement exactly, both in aggregate and node by node

fact.note_on_that_product: this is the pre-event probability of exactly this route, not of the title: the model gave the champion 0.0793 across all routes. A route this long is improbable for anyone, including the favourite

model_miss_diagnosis.what_the_model_got_right_about_the_champ: it did not consider the champion a long shot in absolute terms - 7.9% over eight teams is above the uniform 12.5% floor only for the top four, and the champion ranked fifth. The model placed it mid-field, and a mid-field team won.
model_miss_diagnosis.what_the_model_got_wrong: it ranked the champion fifth of eight by latent strength at serve time, and gave the eventual runner-up more than four times the title probability. The single largest miss on the board is the Grand Final itself, where the model put 0.2747 on the team that won it - the lowest probability it assigned to any realized winner.

hypothesis.hypothesis: recency: a 90-day half-life may discount late-window form too slowly
hypothesis.would_require: multi-event out-of-sample evidence, not one TI
hypothesis.explicitly_not_done: no half-life change is proposed or made

hypothesis.hypothesis: sequential assimilation: updating strengths as the Main Event unfolds might have caught the champion's run
hypothesis.explicitly_not_done: the production forecast is unchanged and is not re-issued

hypothesis.hypothesis: bracket-specific or best-of-5 form is not captured by a map-level rating
roster or patch adaptation inside the event window
hypothesis.would_require: roster and patch metadata the project does not hold

model_miss_diagnosis.prohibited_inference: None of the above may become a TI2027 parameter change on the strength of TI2026. One tournament identifies nothing: with 14 series, a model that is genuinely better and a model that is genuinely worse produce overlapping score distributions. The correct output of this section is a research question with a pre-registered test, not a coefficient.

sequential_posthoc_diagnostic.status: POST-HOC DIAGNOSTIC ONLY; not promoted to any production method

incidents.title: opening bracket seating had no authoritative local provenance
incidents.symptom: the four seeded Main Event pairings entered the model as facts supplied in a request, with nothing in the repository able to confirm them
incidents.root_cause: the saved Valve league feed carries the Playoff graph but every Playoff node in that snapshot has team_id_1 = team_id_2 = 0, so the feed structurally cannot answer who is seated where
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none on the numbers - the pairings were correct - but the claim rested on an unverifiable input, which is a provenance defect whether or not the input is right
incidents.fix: archive a first-party client capture, hash it, transcribe it under review, and derive ti15_results.UBQF from that single transcription so no second seat table can drift from it
incidents.prevention_ti2027: capture and hash the client bracket the day seating is published, before it is needed
incidents.check: ti_predict/seating_evidence.py aborts the run on any hash, byte-count, directory or seat mismatch; tests/test_seating_evidence.py pins it

incidents.title: first-party client evidence closed the seating gap, and the two sources stayed separate
incidents.symptom: not a defect: recorded because the resolution is the reusable part
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none; the slate was unchanged by the archival
incidents.fix: the capture establishes WHO is seated; the Valve feed independently establishes the 14-node graph and the winner/loser edges. Two questions, two artifacts, no circularity - and the eight seated organisations must equal the eight survivors reconstructed from the 44 completed series, which is a real independent check
incidents.prevention_ti2027: keep seating evidence and topology evidence as separate artifacts with separate gates

incidents.title: most current-event timestamps were imputed, not observed
incidents.symptom: only round 1 of the Swiss had a real scheduled_time; rounds 2-6 and the Elimination Round were placed on an assumed two-blocks-per-day cadence
incidents.root_cause: no local source recorded actual start times for those series
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: bounded and reported, not waved away: collapsing every TI15 map onto a single instant moves the block's h90 weight by under 3%, leaves the optimal slate unchanged, and is filed as a sensitivity arm
incidents.fix: label the two provenances separately (official_schedule_feed vs imputed_cadence), count them in the manifest, and run the collapse arm
incidents.prevention_ti2027: capture an authoritative actual start time for every series as it is played; the post-event archive built here shows it is obtainable
incidents.check: the manifest's timestamp_provenance_counts, plus the timestamp sensitivity gate

incidents.title: synthetic result rows contaminated the radiant-side coefficient
incidents.symptom: the estimated side coefficient c came out inflated at 0.1056
incidents.root_cause: the 44 TI15 series were expanded with team_a = series winner, a bookkeeping orientation with no side meaning. 88 of 109 rows therefore had team_a winning by construction, and the side estimator read that as a Radiant advantage
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: c corrected from 0.1056 to 0.0940. Zero change to any strength, zero change to the 14-slot slate - a real bug whose numerical effect happened to be nil
incidents.fix: mark every row with explicit side provenance at construction (radiant_dire vs none) and restrict est_c to genuinely side-labelled rows
incidents.prevention_ti2027: every observation declares its side provenance; no silent semantic overloading of team_a/team_b
incidents.check: ti15_results.side_labelled fails closed on an unmarked row rather than defaulting

incidents.title: a diagnostic was described as something stronger than it was
incidents.symptom: an early-to-late diagnostic was written up as a group-stage-to-playoff replay
incidents.root_cause: the corpus has no stage labels, so a group/playoff split could not be constructed; the population was in fact dominated by season-long leagues, with the top three events carrying about half the evaluation weight
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none - the production path used the plain refit either way
incidents.fix: rename the module to sequential_assimilation, downgrade the claim to a within-league early-to-late diagnostic, and record what was NOT established
incidents.prevention_ti2027: name a diagnostic after what it measures, and record the population it was measured on next to the result
incidents.check: the artifact carries is_a_group_to_playoff_replay=false with its reason, and a not_established field

incidents.title: a candidate set was described as preregistered without a prior artifact
incidents.symptom: the kappa sweep was called preregistered
incidents.root_cause: no timestamped artifact predating the analysis declared that set; a search of the history found none
incidents.fix: relabelled audit-predeclared, with the provenance of the label recorded
incidents.prevention_ti2027: preregistration means a committed, timestamped artifact written before the analysis; anything else gets a weaker word
incidents.check: the artifact stores candidate_set_provenance in plain language

incidents.title: finite-sample headline numbers risked reading as exact
incidents.symptom: expected score, regret and per-node flip costs were quoted to a precision the 1000-draw bootstrap does not support
incidents.root_cause: an exact enumeration (all 2^14 outcomes) wrapped around an approximate distribution, and the exactness of the outer step invited over-reading the inner one
incidents.fix: an explicit approximation block: what is exact given the distribution, what is an estimate, and an instruction to read the numbers from the JSON rather than prose
incidents.prevention_ti2027: state the approximation boundary next to every headline number

incidents.title: canonical identity and client display names had to be separated
incidents.symptom: the same organisations appear as PARIVISION / TEAM VISION, BetBoom Team / BoomBoys, Tundra Esports / Iron Wing / 1w Team depending on the surface
incidents.root_cause: the client, the league feed and third-party databases each use their own display convention, and the model needs one stable key
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none, because the separation was made before submission: the artifact carries both a canonical pick and the client display name to type into the client
incidents.fix: one alias table resolves every surface name to a canonical organisation, and nothing is ever matched by name similarity
incidents.prevention_ti2027: keep the alias table; add new surfaces to it explicitly
incidents.check: ti15_results.canon raises on an unknown identity. The post-event archive is a further check: two independent sources using different conventions both resolve through the same table

incidents.title: selection 810 was a genuine decision-theoretic tie
incidents.symptom: the two candidate picks at selection 810 differed by 0.39 expected points out of roughly 2288, and a 40,000-draw paired bootstrap could not resolve the sign (95% interval about [-127, +121], P(delta>0) = 0.5111)
incidents.root_cause: the underlying series was close to a coin flip and the downstream bracket value of the two branches nearly cancelled
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: the production rule takes the numerical argmax, so Nigma Galaxy was submitted; the artifact records that this is a tie and NOT a demonstration that Nigma was better
incidents.fix: report it as a tie, retain one deterministic client pick, file the paired analysis
incidents.prevention_ti2027: keep the tie language. A tie that is reported as a tie is not a bug when it loses

incidents.title: evidence handling needed fail-closed treatment, not best effort
incidents.symptom: early framings would have let the run proceed on unverified seating
incidents.root_cause: the natural default for a missing artifact is to continue with a warning
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none; the gate was in place before the filed run
incidents.fix: the gate aborts on any mismatch, and the trust boundary (human review of the image-to-text step) is written down rather than implied
incidents.prevention_ti2027: every evidence gate aborts; none warns
incidents.check: tests/test_seating_evidence.py drives the failure paths, not just the happy path

incidents.title: Fantasy statistic observability was incomplete and found late
incidents.symptom: three official scoring statistics - madstones, watchers taken, lotuses grabbed - are not obtainable from any source the project holds
incidents.root_cause: the observability of each official statistic was never enumerated before the value model was built on top of them
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: material and unresolved: the final two-account comparison is decisive on observable data and carries an unbounded unknown term. It closed as PASS_WITH_MATERIAL_UNCERTAINTY
incidents.fix: state the missing terms symbolically, derive the necessary condition for the conclusion to flip, and refuse to substitute a proxy
incidents.prevention_ti2027: build a full statistic x coefficient x source x observability matrix BEFORE any Fantasy optimisation
incidents.check: the Fantasy closure record carries the symbolic equation and the necessary condition rather than a filled-in number

incidents.title: a probability bound was overclaimed and withdrawn
incidents.symptom: First Blood was described as contributing at most 1/10 for an individual
incidents.root_cause: 1/10 is a per-game share across ten players; it is not an upper bound on any individual's rate across a period
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none; no recommendation depended on it
incidents.fix: withdrawn, with no individual upper bound claimed in its place
incidents.prevention_ti2027: a share is not a bound; check which quantity a ratio is a ratio OF
incidents.check: the withdrawn-claims list in the Fantasy closure record

incidents.title: unobservable statistics were extrapolated with an unrelated proxy
incidents.symptom: banner-wide points per scored multiplier unit was used as a per-statistic rate estimator for the three unobservable statistics
incidents.root_cause: an aggregate ratio was treated as if it were a rate; the pressure to fill a hole in a schema produced a number where there was no measurement
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: three claims were withdrawn. The conclusion survived, but only after the invalid support was removed
incidents.fix: withdrawn; the unobservable terms remain symbolic and unbounded
incidents.prevention_ti2027: do not replace missing evidence with a proxy. UNKNOWN is a valid value and an absence of public data is not an event-rate estimate
incidents.check: the withdrawn-claims list, and the rule that unknown is never written as zero

incidents.title: a screenshot transcription was wrong and was caught by re-reading the image
incidents.symptom: a supplied transcription of one banner slot disagreed with the client
incidents.root_cause: hand transcription of a dense UI
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: caught before it propagated. The decisive check was internal: the supplied version contradicted its own displayed multipliers at four of five slots, while the screenshot version reproduced all five exactly
incidents.fix: re-read the image directly and prefer the screenshot over any transcription
incidents.prevention_ti2027: images outrank transcriptions of them, and a transcription that cannot reproduce the displayed derived values is wrong
incidents.check: reproduce every displayed derived quantity from the transcription before using it

incidents.title: the scoring functional is now first-party validated
incidents.symptom: not a defect: the strongest positive result of the closure
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: the optimiser maximised the right thing. Two independent in-client views credit 8 of 14 for 4320 points - the bracket view node by node, the settlement summary view in aggregate - and the production functional recomputes the same result from the frozen slate alone, so the objective that 16,384 slates were ranked by is the objective the client actually pays
incidents.prevention_ti2027: verify the scoring functional against the client BEFORE optimising it, rather than discovering afterwards that it was right
incidents.check: tests/test_postmortem.py asserts the recomputation equals the settlement, both in aggregate and at all 14 nodes

incidents.title: the settlement points figure was initially archived on derivation alone
incidents.symptom: the first archival pass held only the bracket view (ti2026-ev-003). That frame directly shows the 8/14 count, the group-stage 6/16 count and a settlement mark on all 14 nodes, but it does not contain the client's settlement summary modal, so it carries no points figure. An early statement then generalised that absence from the one frame to the client as a whole
incidents.root_cause: incomplete capture coverage - the bracket view and the settlement summary modal are two different client views and only the first was held - compounded by over-generalised transcription wording on the archival side
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none. No prediction or evaluation number changed at any point; 4320 was correct throughout. Only the STRENGTH of its provenance changed: from derivation alone, to derivation plus a direct first-party reading
incidents.fix: two steps. First the wording was corrected so the archive stated a property of the one frame rather than of the client. Then ti2026-ev-006, the settlement summary capture, was archived; it directly shows 8 correct, 6 incorrect and +4,320, and the evaluator now gates the recomputation against BOTH client views
incidents.prevention_ti2027: when one client screen reports several fields the pipeline will quote, capture the view that shows them together. And scope every negative observation to the artifact it was made on - 'this frame does not show X' is verifiable from the bytes, 'the client does not show X' is not
incidents.check: cross_check_settlement requires both ti2026-ev-003 and ti2026-ev-006 to be present and to agree with the recomputation on correct, incorrect and points; a missing or disagreeing view aborts the run
incidents.status: CLOSED - dual first-party/deterministic settlement provenance established

resolution.ev003_remains_valid: the bracket view was never wrong and is not superseded. It remains the only evidence for the per-node marks and for the group-stage count; ev-006 is complementary, not corrective
resolution.operator_report_superseded_by_evidence: while only ev-003 was held, the operator's report of the summary fields was recorded as a report. It is now replaced by the capture itself and is no longer relied on

incidents.title: a secondary source reported the wrong series format
incidents.symptom: a news summary rendered the Main Event series as best-of-5 (3-0, 3-2), which would have made every archived score wrong
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none - caught before archival by cross-checking two hashed sources, both of which give best-of-3 everywhere except the Grand Final
incidents.fix: the archive asserts that each winner's map count equals the clinch number of the node's declared best-of, so a best-of-5 score at a best-of-3 node fails the build
incidents.prevention_ti2027: corroborate every result fact across independent sources and assert format consistency structurally
incidents.check: the outcome build fails closed on a clinch mismatch; sources.json records the rejected source and why

incidents.title: a legacy display-name exposure in frozen pre-event Fantasy state files
incidents.symptom: seven pre-event Fantasy account-state artifacts carry an account holder's client display name inside the rendered compendium_player_title string, which embeds the account name in the title text. The account is a third party, not the operator
incidents.root_cause: the client's title string was transcribed verbatim into the state file. The field was captured for its title semantics; nobody noticed it also carries an identity
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none analytically. It is a privacy defect, not a correctness one, and it is already public: the files were committed and pushed well before the post-event archival
incidents.fix: NOT FIXED, deliberately. Both available remedies are out of scope by instruction and neither would work: editing the files would mutate frozen pre-event evidence, and removing them from history would mean rewriting a published branch, which cannot recall existing clones, forks or caches anyway. Instead the exposure is registered explicitly - an exact file list, enforced by a test - so it is documented and bounded rather than hidden, and cannot spread to a new file
incidents.prevention_ti2027: strip or hash any client string that embeds an account name before it enters a tracked artifact, and scan for identity at capture time rather than at archival time. Transcribe the semantics of a UI string, not the string
incidents.check: tests/test_postmortem.py::test_client_identity_does_not_spread_beyond_the_known_exposure fails on any new tracked file carrying the name, and also fails if the register goes stale

resolution.decision: preserve history; do not rewrite it
rationale: the exposure already exists in published Git history
rewriting history would break published commit identities and the reproduction they anchor
a rewrite could not recall existing clones, forks or caches in any case
the value is a display nickname, not a datum any conclusion depends on
forward controls that stop it spreading are the effective remedy here
resolution.if_removal_is_later_requested: if the affected person explicitly asks for stronger removal, handle it as a separate privacy and history-rewrite operation, not as part of TI2026 scientific archival work

incidents.title: the participant pair is not a unique key for a bracket node
incidents.symptom: the first attempt to place the 14 retrieved series onto the 14 nodes failed: PARIVISION and Team Spirit played each other twice, at the upper bracket semifinal and again in the Grand Final
incidents.root_cause: a double-elimination bracket can rematch any pair; matching on the participant set alone is ambiguous by construction
incidents.impact_on_submitted_decision: none - the build failed closed with a clear message rather than silently taking the first match
incidents.fix: match on the participant set AND the best-of clinch number, and additionally assert that every node starts after both of its input nodes
incidents.prevention_ti2027: never key a bracket node on its participants alone
incidents.check: postmortem.reconcile raises when the match is not unique; a test drives it

known_limitations: N = 1. Fourteen Main Event series, from one tournament, with heavy team overlap between them. Nothing here supports a calibration claim or a comparison against an alternative model.

The probabilities recomputed for actually-played matchups are POINT ESTIMATES from the single frozen serve state. They are not the bootstrap-averaged objects the optimiser maximised, and the two are not interchangeable.
Most TI15 current-event timestamps remain imputed. The post-event archive has observed times for the 14 Main Event series only.
No official Fantasy period settlement was captured, so the Fantasy track's realized outcome is unknown rather than measured.
Three official Fantasy statistics were unobservable from every source held, and no finite bound on their contribution exists in the verified mechanics.

The identity table maps Iron Wing / 1w Team onto the tracked Tundra Esports lineage. That is a pre-existing project convention carried forward unchanged here, not a fact re-verified by this archival phase.
The frozen serve state side-car is reproducible only where the git-ignored rating universe is present. The evaluation itself reads the tracked side-car and does not need it.

The in-client settlement is first-party but singular: there is one capture, and the trust boundary is human review of it. The hash proves the bytes have not changed since review; it cannot prove the review read them correctly.

A legacy display-name exposure exists in frozen pre-event Fantasy state files that were published before this archival began. The operator decided to preserve history rather than rewrite it (INC-19, ACCEPTED_LEGACY_EXPOSURE_PRESERVE_HISTORY); the exposure is registered, bounded to an exact file list, and prevented by test from reaching any new artifact.
reusable_lessons: Verify the scoring functional against the client BEFORE optimising it. TI2026 got this right and only learned afterwards how much was riding on it.

PICK UNCERTAINTY IS NOT PATH UNCERTAINTY. A tie analysis conditional on a matchup answers nothing if that matchup never occurs. Selection 810 was analysed to four decimal places as Nigma versus Liquid; the series actually played there was Liquid versus Falcons.

In a bracket, a wrong pick and a wrong path are different failures. Three of the six misses were nodes where the selected team was not among the two teams that played. Counting them as model errors would triple the apparent local error rate.
Node-winner scoring is far more forgiving than exact-path scoring, and that is worth knowing before choosing an objective: three nodes were credited despite a diverged path.
A tie that is reported as a tie is not a bug when it loses. Selection 810 cost 1080 points and was still the correct call under the information available.
Make a data structure self-checking rather than merely well-formed: the outcome archive is re-derived from the bracket graph on every load, so a corrupted entry fails loudly.
Mark chronology in the data, not only in the directory name. A row carrying a post-event marker is refused by the estimator even if someone reaches past the namespace.
UNKNOWN is a valid value. The most expensive Fantasy error of the year was filling an unknown with a plausible proxy.
Look at the artifact again before recording that you saw something in it.

what_worked.assessment: the model, half-life, lambda and scoring form were fixed before the current-event data arrived and were never reopened. The artifact asserts pipeline identity against the earlier locked group run, so the freeze is checked rather than promised.

the production run recorded network_used=false, odds_used=false and future_main_event_results_used=false, and those fields remain true and unmodified. No odds, market probability or crowd pick entered at any point.

because a coherent 14-slot slate IS one of the 2^14 outcomes, the candidate set equals the outcome space and the optimisation is exact rather than sampled. All 16,384 slates were scored against all 16,384 outcomes.
VALIDATED. Maximising expected official score under node-winner semantics is exactly what the client settled. The recomputation reproduces the client's 8/14 node by node.
expected score is linear in the outcome distribution, so averaging the distribution over bootstrap draws and then optimising is exact rather than an approximation of an average.
whole series were resampled, never individual maps, so a Bo3 could not masquerade as three independent observations.
the topology is read from the saved Valve feed and the seating from a hashed capture, and either one failing aborts the run. Neither was ever hand-entered at the point of use.
six successive scoped audits each found a real defect. Two of them (the side-provenance bug and the cutoff dated after its own run) were genuine correctness issues that no test was catching.
the one near-tie was named as a tie, priced with a paired bootstrap, and submitted by a deterministic rule rather than dressed up as a judgement.
the submitted slate is byte-identical to what it was before this postmortem, and the postmortem asserts that.
kept distinct throughout. The two optima differed at exactly one node, which is precisely the kind of difference that gets lost when the two objectives are conflated.
every raw capture is committed to by hash without publishing the image, and every rename/move was proved byte-preserving.
banner, coach title and team deployment effects were attributed separately and reconciled under one estimator, so the headline difference is explained rather than asserted.

what_this_does_not_prove: One tournament does not validate calibration. Fourteen correlated series cannot distinguish a well-calibrated model from a poorly calibrated one.

8 realized correct against about 5.1 expected does not show the model will outperform again. The model's own pre-event distribution gave a 19.5% chance of scoring at least this well, so the result sits inside the forecast rather than contradicting it.
4320 realized against about 2288 expected does not justify retuning anything. Expected score is an average over a distribution the realization was drawn from.
Team Spirit winning does not justify a shorter half-life, a form term, or any other parameter change. A team the model put fifth of eight won; that is what a 7.9% event looks like when it happens.

The post-hoc sequential-assimilation diagnostic does not validate sequential assimilation. It was chosen after the outcome, scored on 14 non-independent series, and has no interval that would be honest to quote.
Unknown Fantasy statistics must never be silently treated as zero. Exclusion from an estimator and a true value of zero are different claims.
An absence of public data is not an event-rate estimate.
One year's scoring semantics do not carry to the next. The 2027 client must be re-verified before its objective is optimised, however stable the format looks.
The optimiser comparators cannot be ranked on this realization. The max-expected-correct slate scored 1080 more points, from a 0.39-point expected-score difference - noise, resolved by one coin flip.

ti2027_actions.action: record an observed start time, teams, result, map count, sides and roster for every current-event series as it is played
ti2027_actions.why: TI2026 imputed most of its current-event timestamps

ti2027_actions.action: require an explicit side-provenance declaration on every observation used for side-bias estimation
ti2027_actions.why: winner-oriented synthetic rows silently inflated the side coefficient

ti2027_actions.action: build the full Fantasy observability matrix before any Fantasy optimisation, and resolve or explicitly model every unobservable statistic
ti2027_actions.why: three unobservable statistics left the 2026 Fantasy conclusion formally open

ti2027_actions.action: keep raw client captures in the external private archive with hash-before-move discipline; publish hash plus transcription only
ti2027_actions.why: captures are load-bearing evidence and are personally identifying at the same time

ti2027_actions.why: a refit that quietly includes the results it forecast looks excellent and means nothing
